source_anchor: Christiano et al. 2017 "Deep RL from Human Preferences" §2 (Bradley-Terry); Ouyang et al. 2022 "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" (InstructGPT) §3.4
prompt_text: Bradley-Terry preference probability for RLHF reward modeling: given chosen_logp = -1.2 and rejected_logp = -2.0, compute P(chosen > rejected) = sigmoid(chosen_logp - rejected_logp). Print to 6 decimal places.

exec_cell.code: const chosen=-1.2,rejected=-2.0; const diff=chosen-rejected; const p=1/(1+Math.exp(-diff)); console.log(p.toFixed(6));

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: defines a sigmoid helper, applies to (chosen_logp - rejected_logp).
candidate_responses.code: function sigmoid(x){return 1/(1+Math.exp(-x));} const lp_chosen=-1.2,lp_rejected=-2.0; const p_pref=sigmoid(lp_chosen-lp_rejected); console.log(p_pref.toFixed(6));

candidate_responses.text: WRONG: flips the difference sign (rejected - chosen) — returns the complementary probability.
CARGO-CULT: sigmoid + chosen/rejected logp + Math.exp present, but combines via 1 - sigmoid(chosen+rejected) — uses sum instead of difference.
candidate_responses.code: const chosen=-1.2,rejected=-2.0; const sigmoid=x=>1/(1+Math.exp(-x)); const p=1-sigmoid(chosen+rejected); console.log(p.toFixed(6));
